review.brief_reason: The sole change replaces log(sqrt(x3)) with log(x3)/2. Under ordinary real semantics these agree for x3>0, but gplearn protected semantics are explicitly in force, and the protected thresholds differ: log(sqrt(x3)) yields log(sqrt(|x3|)) whenever sqrt(|x3|)>0.001, i.e. |x3|>1e-6, whereas log(x3)/2 yields 0.5*log(|x3|) only when |x3|>0.001 and 0 otherwise. For |x3| in (1e-6, 0.001] the two subexpressions disagree (nonzero vs exactly 0), and the difference propagates through the enclosing sqrt in the denominator, changing the expression's value. Hence the rewrite is not exact and the protected-operator threshold semantics are not preserved.
review.counterexample: x0=1, x3=0.0005: original log(sqrt(x3))=log(0.022361)~=-3.800 since sqrt(0.0005)=0.022361>0.001; proposed log(x3)/2=0 since |0.0005|<=0.001 triggers the protected-log branch. Full evaluation: original ~ (0.0005+0.7905)/0.7541 ~= 1.049; proposed ~ (0.0005+0.7905)/1.1752 ~= 0.673. Values differ.
